costScope: Full ordinary national-recipient gift G retained; f allocates modeled delivery without shrinking denominator. Donated inputs/public leverage disclosed separately. Reuses prior data/us/vision-to-learn-v2.json structure, with fresh original accounts and independently scoped California allocation. Course cost covers core delivery; the 20% outside that allocation covers other recipient activities/support, avoiding a second charge for the same overhead.
geographicAttribution: g is the share of marginal net health benefit accruing to California residents, not office location, cumulative pairs or restricted-program scope. Central .4, favorable .6, adverse .2 are judgment scenarios. Actual g may be 0–1. Multiplying courses by g assumes equal modeled per-course net benefit across regions; regional severity, cost or wear differences would require separate California inputs.
formula: N=G*f/c; k=ln(1+r)+fade; D=(1-exp(-k*T))/k, or T if k=0; L=(1+r)^(-d); q=(p*w*u*D-h)*L; Q_all=(N+M/c)*a*q; Q_CA=(N*g+M/c)*a*q; Price10=10G/Q_CA when positive. ResourceCost=G+M+(N+M/c)*(inkind+school), counting only resources absent from cash c. All finite horizons. fade=0 centrally.
counterfactual: Other donors or reimbursement may fund the same capacity (a); children may obtain adequate correction elsewhere even if the gift adds capacity (p). The finite period ends the modeled advantage over alternative care. These are distinct funding and patient-care counterfactuals.
attribution: Count unique additional delivered child courses, not screenings, exams, multiple pairs or lifetime educational stories. Wear enters once as effective corrected time. No automatic Medicaid matching or causally unmeasured education QALYs.
uncertainty: Conditional model with explicitly judgment-based joint scenarios, not empirically bounded confidence interval. Child utility, marginal California mix and funding additionality dominate. Zero/negative net benefit cannot be ruled out.
nativeOutcomes: Additional unique children receiving a needed correction course; Additional effectively corrected child-years versus alternative care; Measured visual acuity change, distinct from preference-weighted health utility.

inputs.name: f
inputs.rationale: Remaining 20% retained in full gift denominator for support/other activity; not a restricted gift.

inputs.name: c
inputs.unit: cash USD per delivered unique-child care course
inputs.rationale: Not advertised $150 nor accounting expense per pair. Includes delivery/follow-up assumption; $150–400 scenarios.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: Half of financed capacity additional after substitute donors/public funding, not measured.

inputs.name: p
inputs.rationale: Absent adequate alternative correction during horizon; historical Medicaid nonuse is not this probability.

inputs.name: w
inputs.unit: fraction of correction time used effectively
inputs.rationale: Central .6 is constant effective corrected time. In the decay stress .6 is the starting effective-use level, falling exponentially; it is not a measured horizon-average subsequently discounted twice.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: Preference-weighted child utility is missing; 0.005–0.04 sensitivity, not clinical bounds.

inputs.name: T
inputs.rationale: Finite incremental correction period before alternative care/refractive change; no lifetime tail.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: Small allowance for burden/inappropriate correction; could be wrong.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: California share of marginal net health benefit
inputs.rationale: Cumulative California glasses share about44% is context, not marginal evidence. 20–60% cases are analyst scenarios, not bounds.

inputs.name: inkind
inputs.rationale: Separate gross resource sensitivity, not deducted from gift.

inputs.name: M
inputs.unit: hypothetical gross public USD before additionality adjustment
inputs.rationale: Hypothetical gross public receipts attributed to the gift before the shared a adjustment for financial substitution; not already net-additional money. No automatic match is assumed. If evidence identifies net additional funded courses directly, do not apply the same substitution adjustment again.

inputs.name: fade
inputs.rationale: Central 0. Stress ln(2) assumes effective correction begins at .6 and halves over one year; this replaces the constant-use trajectory rather than adding decay to an empirically averaged wear estimate.

inputs.name: school
inputs.rationale: Unknown centrally; $50 gross-resource stress, only if absent from cash course cost.

sensitivity: g alone at .2 or .6 changes central price to about $4.01m or $1.34m; cumulative reach does not resolve it.
p, w and u multiply; sustained correction and child utility dominate alongside funding additionality.
Holding remaining central values, one-year break-even utility for $1m/10Q is approximately .040 and for $100k/10Q approximately .398; solve exact formula including h.
If two pairs per child inflate output counts, inferred unit costs must rise; the model's c is per unique child course.
No public leverage in central. Public payments, donated lenses and shared school resources must not be claimed as free full-resource cost.
Replacement-extra assumes a cost omitted from central c; if central course already includes replacement, use central and do not add it again. The66% transfer is a stress, not CA forecast.
If effective time decays50% annually, central price rises to about$2.78m. Utility.005/.01/.04 gives about$8.19m/$4.04m/$1.00m.
No marginal California allocation, complete financial substitution and net harm are explicitly reproduced.
Positive scenario range cannot establish positive expected impact or donor readiness; no fitted probability distribution is claimed.
